bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing tier-1 relationship with its principal OEM customer (Tata Motors), with multi-product engagement across CV and railway segments
- Raw-material pass-through commercial arrangements - increases in steel and other principal raw-material prices are passed on to customers and decreases passed back, so raw-material volatility is not a direct risk to margin
- Exposure to higher-GVW platforms, where frame and long-member content rises with platform weight, translating a modest unit-volume environment into a meaningful revenue uplift
- Operating leverage from scale, automation and process improvements - productivity per employee rose materially on a base of 91 permanent employees as on 31 March 2026
- Prudent capital structure and deleveraging during the year, supporting operations through cyclical troughs, alongside a liquid treasury surplus
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration - a single OEM accounts for the majority of revenue — The Risk Management Committee lists this as a key risk; revenue from a single major customer accounted for Rs 46,111.30 lakhs of revenue from operations during the year. Mitigation is only partial - a long-standing tier-1 relationship, multi-product engagement, and broadening into adjacent segments (railway fabrication, electric commercial vehicles).
- Demand cyclicality and end-market risk in the Indian CV cycle — The Indian CV cycle is inherently cyclical and end-demand can be affected by macroeconomic conditions, freight-rate movements and upstream cost transmission into truck prices; order flow is also lumpy. Managed through deep customer engagement, multi-product positioning across CV and railway segments, and a prudent capital structure that supports operations through cyclical troughs.
- Indirect raw-material risk through end-demand, rather than direct margin risk — Commercial arrangements with principal customers operate on a pass-through basis - steel and other principal raw-material price increases are passed on to customers and decreases passed back - so raw-material volatility is not a direct risk to margin. The live channel is indirect: sustained raw-material inflation raises truck prices for end customers and softens end-demand, and is monitored under demand cyclicality.
- Technological transition to EV, alternative-fuel and hydrogen-ICE platforms — Management states the long-term shift may render certain frame architectures obsolete or force them to evolve - a structural threat to the Company's core frame and long-member product set. The stated response is investing ahead of these transitions through quality, process and customer-engagement programmes.
- Regulatory transition costs - BS6 Phase II execution, AC-cabin mandates and ADAS rollout — These transitions may require platform-level redesigns and capacity retooling, and regulatory transition costs are listed among the threats as new emission and safety standards come into force.
- Geopolitical and supply-chain disruption risk — Conflict in West Asia (the US-Iran-Israel conflict) and constraints on key shipping routes, notably the Strait of Hormuz, drive volatility in oil, diesel and bought-out component costs and threaten supply of critical bought-out parts. Management describes itself as in a wait-and-watch posture on how this transmits into fleet operating economics and truck buying behaviour.
- Inventory obsolescence in a customer-specific manufacturing model (statutory auditors' key audit matter) — The auditors designated inventory a key audit matter: large quantities held across plants in a customer-specific industry, with slow-moving or damaged inventory arising from model discontinuation or excess production accumulated at different locations, and a possibility of gaps between actual and recorded raw-material consumption across product variants.
- Supplier-ecosystem restructuring at the principal customer's parent group — Announced corporate transactions at the principal customer's parent group will over time reshape the supplier ecosystem and raise the quality bar for tier-1 suppliers. Management frames this as an opportunity for those investing ahead of the curve, but for a supplier with majority revenue from that OEM it is equally a structural re-qualification risk.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections describe no named expansion project, greenfield site or commissioning timeline. Capex intent is stated only qualitatively in the MD&A Outlook: the Company expects to deploy modest capital expenditure entirely from internal accruals in FY 2026-27, and says operating cash generation together with its liquid treasury is expected to comfortably cover all known debt-service obligations and capacity-readiness investments. Related capacity language is defensive rather than additive: regulatory transitions such as BS6 Phase II execution, AC-cabin mandates and ADAS rollout may require platform-level redesigns and capacity retooling, and the Company describes investing ahead of EV, alternative-fuel and hydrogen-ICE transitions through quality, process and customer-engagement programmes rather than through a stated capacity addition. The footprint is described only as a head office at Gurgaon and three plant locations (sites not named), with productivity gains attributed to scale, automation and process improvements implemented over past years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian CV industry returned to a constructive growth phase with overall industry volumes expanding approximately 14% YoY; the M&HCV category, where the Company is most exposed through frames and long members, grew approximately 20%
- Structural premiumisation of the Indian CV fleet - mix-shift from light-tonnage to heavier, more content-rich GVW platforms; frame and long-member content rises with platform weight, so a modest unit-volume environment translates into a meaningful revenue uplift
- Indian CV revenue compounded at approximately 7% per annum over FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25 versus a global CV revenue CAGR of approximately 1%
- Replacement demand catalysed by the BS6 Phase II emission-norm transition, which has driven a sustained re-engineering programme across OEM platforms
- Air-conditioned-cabin mandate for N2/N3 trucks, which is re-engineering the chassis and cabin BOM
- Gradual electrification of public transport, particularly the bus segment driven by State Transport Undertaking demand and pilot programmes for electric intercity buses
- Sustained government infrastructure spending and infrastructure-led demand for tippers and construction-segment trucks
- Announced corporate transactions at the principal customer's parent group, which over time will reshape the supplier ecosystem and raise the quality bar for tier-1 suppliers
- Headwind: US-Iran-Israel conflict and constraints on the Strait of Hormuz introducing fresh risk to crude, diesel and consumables cost, which transmits to fleet operating economics and end-customer truck buying behaviour
- Margin lever: operating leverage from scale, automation and process improvements - EBITDA margin expanded 162 basis points year-on-year, described as the cleanest indicator of operating leverage delivered in the year
- Headwinds flagged: steel cost inflation, supply-chain disruption in critical bought-out parts, CV demand cyclicality and order-flow lumpiness, technological transitions and regulatory transition costs

risks.risk: Customer concentration - a single OEM accounts for the majority of revenue
risks.note: The Risk Management Committee lists this as a key risk; revenue from a single major customer accounted for Rs 46,111.30 lakhs of revenue from operations during the year. Mitigation is only partial - a long-standing tier-1 relationship, multi-product engagement, and broadening into adjacent segments (railway fabrication, electric commercial vehicles).

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality and end-market risk in the Indian CV cycle
risks.note: The Indian CV cycle is inherently cyclical and end-demand can be affected by macroeconomic conditions, freight-rate movements and upstream cost transmission into truck prices; order flow is also lumpy. Managed through deep customer engagement, multi-product positioning across CV and railway segments, and a prudent capital structure that supports operations through cyclical troughs.

risks.risk: Indirect raw-material risk through end-demand, rather than direct margin risk
risks.note: Commercial arrangements with principal customers operate on a pass-through basis - steel and other principal raw-material price increases are passed on to customers and decreases passed back - so raw-material volatility is not a direct risk to margin. The live channel is indirect: sustained raw-material inflation raises truck prices for end customers and softens end-demand, and is monitored under demand cyclicality.

risks.risk: Technological transition to EV, alternative-fuel and hydrogen-ICE platforms
risks.note: Management states the long-term shift may render certain frame architectures obsolete or force them to evolve - a structural threat to the Company's core frame and long-member product set. The stated response is investing ahead of these transitions through quality, process and customer-engagement programmes.

risks.risk: Regulatory transition costs - BS6 Phase II execution, AC-cabin mandates and ADAS rollout
risks.note: These transitions may require platform-level redesigns and capacity retooling, and regulatory transition costs are listed among the threats as new emission and safety standards come into force.

Conflict in West Asia (the US-Iran-Israel conflict) and constraints on key shipping routes, notably the Strait of Hormuz, drive volatility in oil, diesel and bought-out component costs and threaten supply of critical bought-out parts. Management describes itself as in a wait-and-watch posture on how this transmits into fleet operating economics and truck buying behaviour.

risks.risk: Inventory obsolescence in a customer-specific manufacturing model (statutory auditors' key audit matter)
risks.note: The auditors designated inventory a key audit matter: large quantities held across plants in a customer-specific industry, with slow-moving or damaged inventory arising from model discontinuation or excess production accumulated at different locations, and a possibility of gaps between actual and recorded raw-material consumption across product variants.

risks.risk: Supplier-ecosystem restructuring at the principal customer's parent group
risks.note: Announced corporate transactions at the principal customer's parent group will over time reshape the supplier ecosystem and raise the quality bar for tier-1 suppliers. Management frames this as an opportunity for those investing ahead of the curve, but for a supplier with majority revenue from that OEM it is equally a structural re-qualification risk.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Omax Autos is a single-segment tier-1 sheet-metal fabricator making frames, long members and assemblies for Indian commercial-vehicle and railway customers, with a single major customer accounting for Rs 46,111.30 lakhs of FY26 revenue from operations.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and supplies sheet metal components, frames, long members and assemblies for automotive and railway customers within India. Under Ind AS 108 it is engaged in a single business segment and operates primarily under a single geographic location, India, with a long-standing tier-1 relationship with its principal customer Tata Motors in the medium- and heavy-duty commercial-vehicle category. It is broadening into adjacent segments including railway fabrication and electric commercial vehicles.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Sheet metal (single reportable segment):** Sheet metal components, Frames, Long members, Assemblies

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian commercial vehicles, principally M&HCV frames and long members
- Railways (railway fabrication)
- Electric commercial vehicles / bus segment (adjacent segment being broadened into)
- India only - single geographic location, no reportable geographical segments

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian CV industry returned to a constructive growth phase with overall industry volumes expanding approximately 14% YoY; the M&HCV category, where the Company is most exposed through frames and long members, grew approximately 20%
- Structural premiumisation of the Indian CV fleet - mix-shift from light-tonnage to heavier, more content-rich GVW platforms; frame and long-member content rises with platform weight, so a modest unit-volume environment translates into a meaningful revenue uplift
- Indian CV revenue compounded at approximately 7% per annum over FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25 versus a global CV revenue CAGR of approximately 1%
- Replacement demand catalysed by the BS6 Phase II emission-norm transition, which has driven a sustained re-engineering programme across OEM platforms
- Air-conditioned-cabin mandate for N2/N3 trucks, which is re-engineering the chassis and cabin BOM
- Gradual electrification of public transport, particularly the bus segment driven by State Transport Undertaking demand and pilot programmes for electric intercity buses
- Sustained government infrastructure spending and infrastructure-led demand for tippers and construction-segment trucks
- Announced corporate transactions at the principal customer's parent group, which over time will reshape the supplier ecosystem and raise the quality bar for tier-1 suppliers
- Headwind: US-Iran-Israel conflict and constraints on the Strait of Hormuz introducing fresh risk to crude, diesel and consumables cost, which transmits to fleet operating economics and end-customer truck buying behaviour
- Margin lever: operating leverage from scale, automation and process improvements - EBITDA margin expanded 162 basis points year-on-year, described as the cleanest indicator of operating leverage delivered in the year
- Headwinds flagged: steel cost inflation, supply-chain disruption in critical bought-out parts, CV demand cyclicality and order-flow lumpiness, technological transitions and regulatory transition costs

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Broaden beyond the single OEM into adjacent segments - railway fabrication and electric commercial vehicles - as the stated mitigation for customer concentration
- Actively evaluate opportunities to diversify into new business segments to mitigate potential risks and strengthen long-term sustainability, while the core activity remains manufacture and supply of sheet metal components
- Deep customer engagement and multi-product positioning across CV and railway segments, backed by a prudent capital structure that supports operations through cyclical troughs
- Invest ahead of the EV / alternative-fuel / hydrogen-ICE transition through quality, process and customer-engagement programmes so evolving frame architectures do not strand the business
- Position as a tier-1 supplier investing ahead of the curve as announced corporate transactions at the principal customer's parent group reshape the supplier ecosystem and raise the quality bar
- Disciplined cost management, working-capital efficiency and capital-allocation prudence as the response to a fluid geopolitical cost backdrop
- Management focus on improving operational efficiency, maintaining product quality and strengthening customer relationships

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections describe no named expansion project, greenfield site or commissioning timeline. Capex intent is stated only qualitatively in the MD&A Outlook: the Company expects to deploy modest capital expenditure entirely from internal accruals in FY 2026-27, and says operating cash generation together with its liquid treasury is expected to comfortably cover all known debt-service obligations and capacity-readiness investments. Related capacity language is defensive rather than additive: regulatory transitions such as BS6 Phase II execution, AC-cabin mandates and ADAS rollout may require platform-level redesigns and capacity retooling, and the Company describes investing ahead of EV, alternative-fuel and hydrogen-ICE transitions through quality, process and customer-engagement programmes rather than through a stated capacity addition. The footprint is described only as a head office at Gurgaon and three plant locations (sites not named), with productivity gains attributed to scale, automation and process improvements implemented over past years.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-standing tier-1 relationship with its principal OEM customer (Tata Motors), with multi-product engagement across CV and railway segments
- Raw-material pass-through commercial arrangements - increases in steel and other principal raw-material prices are passed on to customers and decreases passed back, so raw-material volatility is not a direct risk to margin
- Exposure to higher-GVW platforms, where frame and long-member content rises with platform weight, translating a modest unit-volume environment into a meaningful revenue uplift
- Operating leverage from scale, automation and process improvements - productivity per employee rose materially on a base of 91 permanent employees as on 31 March 2026
- Prudent capital structure and deleveraging during the year, supporting operations through cyclical troughs, alongside a liquid treasury surplus
